scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: udns (Michael Tokarev) raw-packet routines (udns_parse.c, udns_dn.c, udns_XtoX.c)
family_note: Own C decoder of an asynchronous stub-resolver library; only its documented low-level parsing routines are called and no resolver context is created. The routines return each RR's owner, type, class, TTL and RDATA span; the harness renders RDATA with udns calls (dns_ntop for A/AAAA, dns_getdn + dns_dntop for names, dns_get16 for the MX preference) and reads authority/additional by resetting dnsp_rrl to the section count. udns has accessors for AD and CD but none for the reserved Z bit, so z carries AD and CD only.

name: wahern-dns
license_evidence: LICENSE and the src/dns.c header in the tagged GitHub archive (sha256 39b857be...), checked in the image
input_api: struct dns_packet *dns_p_make(size_t, int *) filled with the message bytes (P->data, P->end), int dns_p_study(struct dns_packet *), dns_header(P) and dns_p_count(P, section), then dns_rr_grep via dns_rr_foreach(&rr, P, .section = ..., .sort = dns_rr_i_packet); names from dns_d_expand, RDATA from dns_any_parse + dns_any_print
documentation_note: The README presents the 'core DNS API built around actual DNS packet' with type-specific RDATA interfaces and dns_rr_foreach/dns_rr_grep iterators; src/dns.h declares struct dns_packet (size, end, data) and the DNS_PUBLIC packet, name, RR and dns_any functions; the release's own parse-packet command (src/dns.c parse_packet) loads raw bytes exactly this way (fread into P->data, set P->end, then dns_rr_foreach). The doc/dns.tex guide in the release does not cover the packet API.
scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family_note: Own C decoder of a non-blocking stub and recursive resolver library in one file; only the packet, name and RR routines are called and no resolver, resolv.conf or hosts object is created. It shares no code with c-ares, ldns/gldns, libknot, udns or getdns. Debian does not package dns.c itself; belle-sip and lua-cqueues embed copies (both excluded in round 4), which do not give dns.c a Debian source identity. The harness lower-cases names, adds a trailing dot when missing, and splits dns_any_print's MX text to normalise the exchange; every value comes from the library. struct dns_header exposes the three bits after RA as one field, so z carries Z, AD and CD.
